newsitem.title: USA: W.Virginia plans to appeal tobacco suit dismissal.
newsitem.headline: W.Virginia plans to appeal tobacco suit dismissal.

text.p: The West Virginia attorney general's office plans to appeal last week's dismissal of most of the state's lawsuit against tobacco companies that seeks to recover public health costs incurred from treating smoking-related illnesses.

"It's our intent (to appeal)," Deborah McHenry, deputy managing attorney general, said on Tuesday. "It's our opinion that the decision of the circuit court judge was wrong based on both fact and law."

Kanawha County Circuit Judge Irene C. Berger last Thursday dismissed all of the state's claims for fraud, negligence, unjust enrichment and conspiracy. She ruled that the state attorney general's office lacked authority from the state legislature to pursue the claim.
Berger let stand allegations that the tobacco industry's manufacturing and marketing of cigarettes violated state consumer protection and antitrust statutes.
A hearing to determine whether the attorney general can proceed with those claims is scheduled for Thursday in Berger's courtroom.

West Virginia's lawsuit was originally filed in September 1994 against 17 tobacco companies and seeks unspecified damages. At least 20 other states have filed lawsuits against tobacco companies that seek to recover public health costs from treating smoking-related illnesses.
McHenry said smoking-related illnesses kill about 4,000 West Virginia residents each year and treating sick smokers costs the state in excess of $100 million annually.
